title: DDS physiology photographed fragment
note: Single cropped image forwarded from a 2024-07-20 post; DDS labeling is archive provenance. Nine visible items retained, including two cardiovascular questions. Original question numbers are not reliably visible; fragment-N identifies their top-to-bottom order. Circled marks and ticks are unofficial. This fragment is not default-eligible.

questions.prompt: Which one the following airways is part of anatomical dead space?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Main bronchi conduct air without direct gas exchange and belong to anatomical dead space. Original question-number margin is clipped; fragment number is a local sequence identifier.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following agent leads to bronchodilation?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Beta-2 stimulation dilates bronchioles. The circled source option is M3, which instead promotes cholinergic contraction.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is TRUE about bronchial circulation?
options: Is a part of the low-pressure circulation
Supplies blood flow to conducting zone
Provides pulmonary capillary perfusion for gas exchange
The bronchial artery consists of deoxygenated blood
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Bronchial circulation is systemic oxygenated high-pressure supply to supporting tissues and conducting airways.

questions.prompt: Which of the following occur during normal expiration?
options: Diaphragm contracts and pleural pressure increases
External intercostal contract and alveolar pressure increase
Diaphragm relaxes and pleural and alveolar pressures decrease
Diaphragm relaxes and alveolar pressure increases
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Normal expiration follows diaphragm relaxation and elastic recoil, producing transient positive alveolar pressure. Source C reverses the pressure changes.

questions.prompt: In which zone, blood flow is established during both of systole and diastole periods?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Zone-3 vascular pressures remain above alveolar pressure, allowing continuous flow.

questions.prompt: What is the total amount of O2 in systemic arterial blood in healthy condition?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: About 19.8-20 mL O2/dL is the conventional reference for normal hemoglobin concentration and saturation. It is a teaching value rather than a fixed value for every healthy person.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following centers controls inspiration and respiratory rhythm?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: DRG is the traditional expected answer for quiet inspiratory drive; the source circles pneumotaxic center. Modern rhythm generation involves distributed networks including pre-Botzinger neurons.

questions.prompt: Which part of vessels have highest total cross section area?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The aggregate cross-sectional area is greatest across the capillary network. This cardiovascular physiology item is preserved for complete source transcription and is outside respiratory default practice.

questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: mmHg is the pressure unit among the choices; the others alone are length or volume units. This basic cardiovascular item is preserved but outside respiratory default practice.
